summary: Blueprint for modular symbols and analytic p-adic L-functions of modular forms. L0 is source-decomposed (checkpoints 1–2): Pollack–Stevens' Hom-side modular symbols Symb_Γ(V) = Hom_Γ(Div⁰(P¹(ℚ)), V) for arbitrary coefficient modules, with Hecke, diamond and involution actions, the Manin and fundamental-domain descriptions, boundary symbols and the integral exact sequence 0 → V^Γ → BSymb → Symb → H¹(Γ, V) → ⊕ H¹(Γ_c, V), parabolic cohomology, descent, symbols with character, the period symbol ψ_f, the Eichler–Shimura isomorphism (Wiese's proof) and one-dimensional newform eigenspaces. Div⁰, Manin's theorem, the homological module 𝕄 and the period-map analysis are imported from Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 8 rather than re-planned. Pollack–Stevens Theorem 2.6/Corollary 2.7 print the D∞ relation with the wrong sign (sourceIssues E1). Stages L1–L4 remain. Checkpoint 3 plans L1 (6 nodes): period lines and periods after a choice of basis, saturated integral lattices with periods canonical up to 𝒪^×, the twisted Mellin formula (Σχ(a)·2πi∫_{i∞}^{a/m} f(z)(z − a/m)^j dz = τ(χ)j!/(−2πi)^j L(f, χ̄, j+1), checked numerically), algebraicity with the parity sign (−1)^{k−j}χ(−1), L-functions of p-stabilized forms, and the exact comparison with RJW Theorem B.1.

nodes.title: Modular symbols
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and a right ℤ[Γ]-module V, Symb_Γ(V) is the group of additive maps φ : Δ₀ → V with φ(γD) = φ(D)|γ^{-1} for all γ ∈ Γ, D ∈ Δ₀, where Δ₀ = Div⁰(P¹(ℚ)) is the degree-zero divisor module with its action of GL₂⁺(ℚ) by linear fractional transformations (imported from ModularForms Layer 8, see requests). In the formal version V carries the left representation ρ(γ)v = v|γ^{-1}, and the condition reads φ(γD) = ρ(γ)φ(D); equivalently Symb_Γ(V) = Hom_{ℤ[Γ]}(Δ₀, V).
hypotheses: Γ acts on Δ₀ through SL₂(ℤ) → GL₂(ℚ).
Left/right conventions: Pollack–Stevens' right action v|γ is recorded as the left representation v ↦ v|γ^{-1}.
proofSteps: Define symbols Γ ρ as the additive subgroup of maps Δ₀ → V satisfying the equivariance; closure under sums and negatives is immediate.
A modular symbol is determined by its values on the unimodular divisors {γ0} − {γ∞}, because these generate Δ₀ (Manin's theorem, imported from ModularForms Layer 8).
acceptance: Symb_{SL₂(ℤ)}(ℤ) = 0: by the Manin relations φ({0} − {∞}) = v satisfies 2v = 0 and 3v = 0.
Symb_{Γ₀(11)}(ℤ) has rank 3 = 2g + (c − 1), with genus g = 1 and c = 2 cusps.
When the orders of torsion elements act invertibly on V, Symb_Γ(V) ≅ H¹_c(H/Γ, Ṽ) (Pollack–Stevens, citing Ash–Stevens [2, Prop. 4.2]); planned as remaining work.

nodes.title: ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] is free over ℤ[Γ]
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ G of finite index in a group G (here G = SL₂(ℤ) or PSL₂(ℤ)), ℤ[G] is a free left ℤ[Γ]-module with basis any set of right coset representatives {g_j} of Γ\G; consequently Hom_{ℤ[Γ]}(ℤ[G], V) ≅ ∏_j V by F ↦ (F(g_j))_j.

proofSteps: SL₂(ℤ) = ⊔_i Γ g_i gives ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] = ⊕_i ℤ[Γ]g_i, and γ g_i ↦ (γ, i) is a bijection Γ × (Γ\SL₂(ℤ)) → SL₂(ℤ).

Combined with the Manin relations this gives the ℤ[Γ]-presentation of Δ₀ by coset generators.

nodes.title: The coefficient modules V_k = Sym^k
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring R and k ≥ 0, V_k(R) is the R-module of homogeneous polynomials of degree k in X, Y, with the right action of integral matrices of nonzero determinant (P|γ)(X, Y) = P((X, Y)·γ*) = P(dX − cY, −bX + aY) for γ = (a b; c d), γ* its adjugate; restricted to Γ it gives the left representation γ ↦ (P ↦ P|γ^{-1}).

proofSteps: V_k(R) := MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) R k; P|γ := aeval of the substitution X ↦ dX − cY, Y ↦ −bX + aY, which preserves degree k.
Right action: (γδ)* = δ*γ* gives P|(γδ) = (P|γ)|δ.

proofSteps: Closure: the lower-left entry of a product is c a′ + d c′ ≡ 0 mod N, and the upper-left entry a a′ + b c′ ≡ a a′ mod N is prime to N; determinants multiply.

nodes.title: Hecke operators on modular symbols
nodes.statement: For V with a right Σ₀(N)-action extending its Γ₀(N)-action, and φ ∈ Symb_{Γ₀(N)}(V): (φ|δ)(D) := φ(δD)|δ; for a prime ℓ ∤ N, φ|T_ℓ := φ|(ℓ 0; 0 1) + Σ_{a=0}^{ℓ−1} φ|(1 a; 0 ℓ); for q | N, φ|U_q := Σ_{a=0}^{q−1} φ|(1 a; 0 q). These preserve Symb_{Γ₀(N)}(V) and commute.
hypotheses: V's Γ₀(N)-action is the restriction of the Σ₀(N)-action.
proofSteps: The listed matrices are representatives of Γ₀(N)\Γ₀(N)(ℓ 0; 0 1)Γ₀(N) (resp. for U_q); right multiplication by γ ∈ Γ₀(N) permutes the cosets, so Σ φ|α_i is again Γ₀(N)-invariant.

The operators come from an action of the Γ₀(N) Hecke ring of double cosets on Symb_{Γ₀(N)}(V), with T_ℓ the class of Γ₀(N)(ℓ 0; 0 1)Γ₀(N); commutativity follows from commutativity of that ring (Tau Ceti HeckeRing.GL2.commRingHeckeRingGamma0).
acceptance: On Symb_{Γ₀(11)}(ℤ), T_2 has characteristic polynomial (x − 3)(x + 2)²: eigenvalue 3 on the boundary (Eisenstein) part and a₂(11a) = −2 on the plus and minus parts.
On the same space T_3 has characteristic polynomial (x − 4)(x + 1)².

nodes.title: Modular symbols as functions on cosets (Manin symbols, cohomological side)
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, let {g_j} be right coset representatives of Γ\SL₂(ℤ), and let V be a right ℤ[Γ]-module. For g ∈ SL₂(ℤ) write g = γ_g g_{j(g)} with γ_g ∈ Γ. The map φ ↦ (v_j)_j, v_j := φ({g_j 0} − {g_j ∞}), is an isomorphism from Symb_Γ(V) onto the families (v_j) ∈ ∏_j V such that, for every j, with x(g) := v_{j(g)}|γ_g^{-1}: x(g_j) + x(g_j σ) = 0, x(g_j) + x(g_j τ) + x(g_j τ²) = 0, and x(g_j) = x(−g_j), where σ = (0 −1; 1 0) and τ = (0 −1; 1 −1).
hypotheses: Γ has finite index in SL₂(ℤ).
The relation list is the image of Manin's kernel ℤ[G](1 + σ) + ℤ[G](1 + τ + τ²) + ℤ[G](1 − (−1)) under the coset basis.
proofSteps: By Manin's theorem (requested from ModularForms Layer 8) d : ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] → Δ₀, g ↦ {g0} − {g∞}, is surjective with kernel the left ideal I generated by 1 + σ, 1 + τ + τ² and 1 − (−1); so Symb_Γ(V) = Hom_{ℤ[Γ]}(ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)]/I, V).
A ℤ[Γ]-linear map F : ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] → V is determined by the values F(g_j) on the coset basis (coset-basis), with F(γ g_j) = F(g_j)|γ^{-1}.
F kills I iff F(g(1 + σ)) = F(g(1 + τ + τ²)) = F(g(1 − (−1))) = 0 for every g; by Γ-equivariance it suffices to take g = g_j, and F(g) = x(g) by the first step.
Hence evaluation at the unimodular divisors d(g_j) identifies Symb_Γ(V) with the stated set of families.
acceptance: For Γ = SL₂(ℤ) (one coset, g₁ = 1) and V = ℤ with trivial action the conditions read 2v = 0 and 3v = 0, so Symb_{SL₂(ℤ)}(ℤ) = 0.
For Γ = Γ₀(11) (12 cosets) and V = ℤ the solution module has rank 3, matching Pollack's worked Γ₀(11) example.
Changing the coset representatives changes the isomorphism by the corresponding γ-twists and not its image.

nodes.title: A modular symbol is determined by its values on the fundamental-domain generators
nodes.statement: Let Γ ⊊ PSL₂(ℤ) have finite index and contain T = (1 1; 0 1), and let D₁, …, D_t, D_∞, D′₁, …, D′_s, D″₁, …, D″_r be the generators of Δ₀ read off a Farey fundamental domain, with the matrices γ_i, γ′_i (order 2) and γ″_i (order 3) in Γ (Pollack–Stevens §§2.4–2.5; the presentation is imported from ModularForms Layer 8). For a right Γ-module V and v₁, …, v_t, v_∞, v′₁, …, v′_s, v″₁, …, v″_r ∈ V with v_∞|Δ = Σ_i v_i|(1 − γ_i) − Σ_i v′_i − Σ_i v″_i (Δ := T − 1), v′_i|(1 + γ′_i) = 0 and v″_i|(1 + γ″_i + γ″_i²) = 0, there is a unique φ ∈ Symb_Γ(V) with φ(D_i) = v_i, φ(D_∞) = v_∞, φ(D′_i) = v′_i and φ(D″_i) = v″_i; every φ arises so. This is Pollack–Stevens' Corollaries 2.7 and 2.10 with the sign of the D_∞ relation corrected (sourceIssues E1).
hypotheses: Γ has finite index in PSL₂(ℤ), contains T and is proper (for the three-torsion version); for Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) apply it to the image Γ̄ and to V^{⟨−1⟩∩Γ}, since −1 acts trivially on Δ₀.
The relations among the generators are Σ_i (γ_i^{-1} − 1)D_i + Σ_i D′_i + Σ_i D″_i = (1 − T^{-1})D_∞, (1 + γ′_i)D′_i = 0 and (1 + γ″_i + γ″_i²)D″_i = 0.
proofSteps: Theorem 2.6/2.9 of Pollack–Stevens, as corrected (request to ModularForms Layer 8): Δ₀ is generated over ℤ[Γ] by the D's with the displayed relations. The relation is derived from the printed boundary relation (1 − T^{-1})e_∞ + Σ(1 − γ_i^{-1})e_i + Σ e′_i ∈ J on p. 11 by applying ∂, with D′_i = −∂(e′_i).
A ℤ[Γ]-linear map out of a presented module is the same as values on the generators satisfying the relations.

Apply φ(γD) = φ(D)|γ^{-1} to the first relation: Σ v_i|(γ_i − 1) + Σ v′_i + Σ v″_i = v_∞ − v_∞|T = −v_∞|Δ; the torsion relations give v′_i|(1 + γ′_i) = 0 and v″_i|(1 + γ″_i + γ″_i²) = 0 because γ′_i, γ″_i have order 2, 3 in PSL₂(ℤ).

nodes.title: The boundary exact sequence for modular symbols
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and any right ℤ[Γ]-module V the sequence 0 → V^Γ → BSymb_Γ(V) → Symb_Γ(V) → H¹(Γ, V) → ⊕_{c ∈ Γ\P¹(ℚ)} H¹(Γ_c, V) is exact, where the first map sends v to the constant function, the second is res, the third is δ (symbols-to-cohomology) and the last is the product of the restrictions to the cusp stabilisers (choosing representatives).
hypotheses: No invertibility hypothesis: the sequence is exact integrally.
The cusp stabilisers Γ_c are the conjugates of Γ ∩ ⟨±T⟩, cyclic modulo ±1.
proofSteps: Apply Hom_{ℤ[Γ]}(−, V) to 0 → Δ₀ → ℤ[P¹(ℚ)] → ℤ → 0 (degree sequence, imported with Δ₀) and take the long exact Ext sequence.

ℤ[P¹(ℚ)] = ⊕_c ℤ[Γ/Γ_c] = ⊕_c Ind_{Γ_c}^Γ ℤ, so Ext¹_{ℤ[Γ]}(ℤ[P¹(ℚ)], V) = ⊕_c Ext¹_{ℤ[Γ_c]}(ℤ, V) = ⊕_c H¹(Γ_c, V) (Shapiro/Eckmann), and the map from H¹(Γ, V) is restriction.
Identify the connecting homomorphism with δ up to sign (symbols-to-cohomology, last step).

nodes.title: Descent of modular symbols from a normal subgroup
nodes.statement: Let Γ′ ⊴ Γ be finite-index subgroups of SL₂(ℤ) and V a right ℤ[Γ]-module. Then Γ/Γ′ acts on Symb_{Γ′}(V) by φ ↦ φ|γ, and Symb_Γ(V) = Symb_{Γ′}(V)^{Γ/Γ′}, integrally and with no division. If [Γ : Γ′] is invertible on V, then restriction gives H¹(Γ, V) ≅ H¹(Γ′, V)^{Γ/Γ′} and H¹_par(Γ, V) ≅ H¹_par(Γ′, V)^{Γ/Γ′}, and Symb_Γ(V) is a direct summand of Symb_{Γ′}(V) via the averaging idempotent e = [Γ:Γ′]^{-1} Σ_{γ ∈ Γ/Γ′} (·)|γ.
hypotheses: Γ′ normal in Γ of finite index. In applications Γ′ = Γ ∩ Γ₁(M) with M ≥ 4 is torsion-free, so all stabilisers in H are trivial.
Only the second and third statements use that [Γ : Γ′] is invertible; the first holds over ℤ. Dividing by the order of an elliptic stabiliser is never used.
proofSteps: (φ|γ)(D) = φ(γD)|γ is well defined on Symb_{Γ′}(V) because Γ′ is normal, and Γ′ acts trivially; a Γ′-symbol fixed by all of Γ is a Γ-symbol, and conversely.

Inflation–restriction: 0 → H¹(Γ/Γ′, V^{Γ′}) → H¹(Γ, V) → H¹(Γ′, V)^{Γ/Γ′} → H²(Γ/Γ′, V^{Γ′}); the outer groups are killed by [Γ : Γ′], hence vanish when it is invertible (H1InfRes_exact and the corestriction–restriction identity).
The same argument at every cusp stabiliser shows that the restriction isomorphism preserves the parabolic subspaces.
e is an idempotent onto the invariants when [Γ : Γ′] is invertible.

nodes.statement: Let V be a right ℤ[Γ₀(N)]-module (for instance the restriction of a right Σ₀(N)-module). nodes.statement: For finite-index Γ, a left ℤ[Γ]-module W, and an abelian group M with trivial action, give Hom_ℤ(W, M) the right action (f|γ)(w) = f(γw). Then Symb_Γ(Hom_ℤ(W, M)) ≅ Hom_ℤ((Δ₀ ⊗ W)_Γ, M), φ ↦ ([D ⊗ w] ↦ φ(D)(w)), naturally in W and M. nodes.title: The invariant pairing between V_k and Sym^k
nodes.statement: Let W_k(R) = R[X, Y]_k with the left action (γ·Q)(X, Y) = Q((X, Y)γ) and V_k(R) the same module with the right action (P|γ)(X, Y) = P((X, Y)γ*), γ* = adj γ (polynomial-coefficients). If k! is invertible in R there is a unique R-bilinear pairing ⟨ , ⟩ : V_k(R) × W_k(R) → R with ⟨(uX + vY)^k, (sX + tY)^k⟩ = (ut − vs)^k for all u, v, s, t ∈ R; on monomials ⟨X^iY^{k−i}, X^jY^{k−j}⟩ = (−1)^{k−i}/C(k, i) if i + j = k and 0 otherwise. It is perfect and satisfies ⟨P|γ, Q⟩ = ⟨P, γ·Q⟩ for every integral γ with det γ ≠ 0; so P ↦ ⟨P, ·⟩ is an isomorphism of right modules V_k(R) ≅ Hom_R(W_k(R), R). nodes.title: The period symbol of a cusp form
nodes.statement: For k ≥ 0, Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and f ∈ S_{k+2}(Γ), ψ_f : Δ₀ → V_k(ℂ) is the additive map with ψ_f({s} − {r}) = 2πi ∫_r^s f(z)(zX + Y)^k dz (geodesic path in H, improper at cusps). nodes.title: Dimension of parabolic cohomology
nodes.statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0 and Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index μ in PSL₂(ℤ) (index of the image) with trivial stabilisers in H (e.g. Γ₁(N), N ≥ 4), with ν∞ cusps. Then dim_K H¹(Γ, V_k(K)) = (k + 1)μ/6 + δ_{k,0} and dim_K H¹_par(Γ, V_k(K)) = (k + 1)μ/6 − ν∞ + 2δ_{k,0}.
hypotheses: Characteristic 0 (the computation of T-invariants and coinvariants of V_k needs k!N to be invertible).
Trivial stabilisers, so Coind(V_k) has no invariants for the finite subgroups ⟨σ⟩, ⟨τ⟩ beyond those computed by Mayer–Vietoris.

Mayer–Vietoris for PSL₂(ℤ) = ⟨σ⟩ ∗ ⟨τ⟩: 0 → M^G → M^{⟨σ⟩} ⊕ M^{⟨τ⟩} → M → H¹(G, M) → 0, with M^{⟨σ⟩} and M^{⟨τ⟩} of dimensions μ(k+1)/2 and μ(k+1)/3 when the stabilisers are trivial.
dim V_k(K)^Γ = δ_{k,0} and, at each cusp, dim H¹(⟨T^n⟩, V_k(K)) = dim V_k(K)^{⟨T^n⟩} = 1 (Wiese Lemma 4.15).

nodes.title: The Eichler–Shimura isomorphism
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) be of finite index and k ≥ 0. The map S_{k+2}(Γ) ⊕ \overline{S_{k+2}(Γ)} → H¹_par(Γ, V_k(ℂ)), (f, \bar g) ↦ δ(ψ_f) + \overline{δ(ψ_g)}, is an isomorphism compatible with the Hecke and diamond operators; for each sign ±, f ↦ δ((1 ± ι)ψ_f) is an isomorphism S_{k+2}(Γ) ≅ H¹_par(Γ, V_k(ℂ))^± when ι normalises Γ. Via symbols-mod-eisenstein the same holds for Symb_Γ(V_k(ℂ))/Eis_Γ(V_k(ℂ)).
hypotheses: For Γ = Γ₁(N), N ≥ 4 (trivial stabilisers) this is Wiese Theorem 6.15; general Γ follows by symbols-level-descent from Γ ∩ Γ₁(M), M ≥ 4, over ℂ.
Uses the positive definite Petersson product on cusp forms (Tau Ceti CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosets_definite) and the dimension formula for S_{k+2}(Γ₁(N)) (request to ModularForms 10C).
proofSteps: Well defined and parabolic: δ(ψ_f) is a cocycle whose restriction to every cusp stabiliser is a coboundary (Wiese Propositions 6.7, 6.9).

Injective: the cup product and the invariant pairing on V_k give a pairing on H¹_par (Wiese Proposition 6.13, 6 invertible) which evaluates on (δψ_f, \overline{δψ_f}) to a nonzero multiple of the Petersson norm of f (Proposition 6.14); positivity of the Petersson norm forces f = 0; likewise for \bar g.
Dimensions: dim H¹_par(Γ₁(N), V_k(ℂ)) = (k + 1)μ/6 − ν∞ + 2δ_{k,0} (parabolic-cohomology-dimension) equals 2 dim S_{k+2}(Γ₁(N)) by the dimension formula; so the injective map is bijective.

Hecke compatibility: Wiese Proposition 7.24 (the Hecke operators on H¹ match slash operators through the period integrals), and ⟨d⟩ likewise; the ± statements follow as in Wiese Corollary 7.33 by dimension.
Descent to general Γ: apply symbols-level-descent with the Γ/Γ′-action, over ℂ.

nodes.title: Newform eigenspaces of modular symbols are one-dimensional
nodes.statement: Let f ∈ S_{k+2}(Γ₁(N)) be a newform of level N with character ε and coefficient field K_f = ℚ(a_n(f), ε). For each sign ±, the subspace Symb_{Γ₁(N)}(V_k(K_f))^±[ε][λ_f] on which T_ℓ acts by a_ℓ(f) for every prime ℓ ∤ N is one-dimensional over K_f, it meets Eis_{Γ₁(N)} trivially, and after ⊗ℂ it is spanned by (1 ± ι)ψ_f.

nodes.title: Period lines and periods
nodes.statement: Let f ∈ S_{k+2}(Γ₁(N)) be a normalized newform with character ε_N and coefficient field K_f = ℚ(a_n(f), ε_N), with a fixed embedding K_f ↪ ℂ. A period exists only after a basis is chosen: for φ^± ∈ L_f^± ∖ {0}, Ω_f^±(φ^±) ∈ ℂ^× is the scalar with ψ_f^± = Ω_f^±(φ^±)·φ^±. Replacing φ^± by λφ^± (λ ∈ K_f^×) replaces Ω_f^± by λ^{−1}Ω_f^± and every period-normalized value by λ times itself.

nodes.title: Saturated integral lattices and integral periods

nodes.title: The twisted Mellin formula for modular symbols
nodes.statement: Let f = Σ a_n q^n ∈ S_{k+2}(Γ₁(N)), χ a primitive Dirichlet character of conductor m ≥ 1, τ(χ) = Σ_{a mod m} χ(a)e^{2πia/m}, L(f, χ, s) = Σ χ(n)a_n n^{−s} (entire, in the convention of Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 7), and 0 ≤ j ≤ k. Then, along vertical paths, Σ_{a mod m} χ(a)·2πi∫_{i∞}^{a/m} f(z)(z − a/m)^j dz = τ(χ)·j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f, χ̄, j+1). Equivalently, with χ̄ for χ, Σ_a χ̄(a)·2πi∫_{i∞}^{a/m} f(z)(z − a/m)^j dz = τ(χ̄)·j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f, χ, j+1). In symbol form, Σ_a χ(a)·λ_{j,a/m}(ψ_f({a/m} − {∞})) = τ(χ)·j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f, χ̄, j+1) with λ_{j,x}(P) = (j!/k!)(∂_Y^{k−j}P)(1, −x). For m = 1: 2πi∫_{i∞}^0 f(z)z^j dz = j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f, j+1).
hypotheses: The Mellin transform, entire continuation of L(g, s) for cusp forms g, and twisted L-functions are imported from Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 7 (RS-08).

Every convention that changes the formula is explicit. The sum against χ(a) produces L(f, χ̄), not L(f, χ). The Gauss sum is τ(χ) = Σχ(a)e^{2πia/m}. The path runs from i∞ to a/m; reversing it changes the sign. Using −a/m multiplies by χ(−1). The factor 2πi sits in ψ_f, with j!/(−2πi)^j on the right, and not (2πi)^{j+1}.
proofSteps: Birch's lemma: Σ_{a mod m} χ̄(a)e^{2πina/m} = χ(n)τ(χ̄) for primitive χ and every n, so f_χ := Σχ(n)a_n q^n = τ(χ̄)^{−1}Σ_a χ̄(a) f(z + a/m).

Mellin: for a cusp form g, 2πi∫_{i∞}^{0} g(z)z^j dz = −2πi·i^{j+1}∫_0^∞ g(iy)y^j dy = −2πi·i^{j+1}·j!(2π)^{−j−1}L(g, j+1) = j!/(−2πi)^j·L(g, j+1). The integral converges at both ends because g vanishes at every cusp.
Apply this to g = f_χ and substitute w = z + a/m: Σ_a χ̄(a)·2πi∫_{i∞}^{a/m} f(w)(w − a/m)^j dw = τ(χ̄)·j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f, χ, j+1). Then exchange χ and χ̄.

nodes.title: Algebraicity of critical values with the parity sign
nodes.statement: Let T_{j,χ}(ψ) := Σ_{a mod m} χ(a)·λ_{j,a/m}(ψ({a/m} − {∞})) and ε := (−1)^{k−j}χ(−1). Then T_{j,χ}(ψ|ι) = εT_{j,χ}(ψ), so T_{j,χ} vanishes on the −ε eigenspace and T_{j,χ}(ψ_f) = ½T_{j,χ}(ψ_f^ε). For any basis φ^ε of L_f^ε, τ(χ)·j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f, χ̄, j+1)/Ω_f^ε(φ^ε) = ½T_{j,χ}(φ^ε) ∈ K_f(χ), for 0 ≤ j ≤ k and χ primitive. The sign is selected by parity: when k is even (for instance trivial character), ε = (−1)^jχ(−1).
hypotheses: The action (P|γ)(X, Y) = P((X, Y)γ*) with γ* = adj γ, and (φ|ι)(D) = φ(ιD)|ι, are L0's; other conventions change ε by a sign that must be tracked.
proofSteps: ι({a/m} − {∞}) = {−a/m} − {∞}; substituting a ↦ −a gives T_{j,χ}(ψ|ι) = (−1)^{k−j}χ(−1)T_{j,χ}(ψ).
T_{j,χ}((1 ± ι)ψ) = (1 ± ε)T_{j,χ}(ψ), which is 2T(ψ) for the sign ε and 0 for the other.
ψ_f^ε = Ω^εφ^ε with φ^ε K_f-rational, and λ_{j,a/m} has rational coefficients, so T_{j,χ}(φ^ε) ∈ K_f(χ). Conclude with twisted-mellin-formula.

nodes.title: The RJW B.1 interpolation formula in the period dictionary
nodes.statement: RJW Theorem B.1 prints, for f of weight k+2 and level Γ₀(N) with p | N, U_p-eigenvalue α_p with v_p(α_p) < k+1, χ of conductor p^n and 0 ≤ j ≤ k: L_p^an(f, χ̄, j+1) = ∫_{ℤ_p^×}χ(x)x^j·L_p^an(f) = −α_p^{−n}(1 − χ(p)p^j/α_p)·G(χ)·j!·p^{nj}/(2πi)^{j+1}·L(f, χ̄, j+1)/Ω_f^±, with G(χ) = τ(χ). In the dictionary of twisted-mellin-formula, put I_j(x) := 2πi∫_{i∞}^{x} f(z)(z − x)^j dz. For n ≥ 1 the right side equals exactly (−1)^{j+1}/(2πi·Ω_f^±)·α_p^{−n}p^{nj}Σ_{a mod p^n}χ(a)I_j(a/p^n), and equally −ε(−1)^k/(2πi·Ω_f^±)·α_p^{−n}p^{nj}Σ_aχ(a)I_j(−a/p^n), where ε = (−1)^{k−j}χ(−1). Only the second prefactor depends on the sign ε alone. So B.1 holds with a j-independent period Ω_f^± exactly when the distribution is normalized through the cusps −a/p^n, or equivalently through x ↦ −x: this is the normalization L2 must fix. For n = 0 and f = f_α the p-stabilization of f°, B.1 reads −(1 − p^j/α)(1 − ε_N(p)p^{k−j}/α)·j!/(2πi)^{j+1}·L(f°, j+1)/Ω^±.
hypotheses: This node proves the classical side of the comparison. The existence and uniqueness of L_p^an(f) as a locally analytic distribution of growth v_p(α_p) (Manin, Amice–Vélu, Višik; Pollack–Stevens) is stage L2.

The stage text quotes B.1 with 'L(f,chi,j+1)'. RJW's printed B.1 has χ̄ both in L_p^an(f, χ̄, j+1) and in L(f, χ̄, j+1); this was read on the page image, because text extraction drops the bar. B.1 as printed therefore agrees with the dictionary and needs no source correction; the stage's transcription drops the bar.
proofSteps: Substitute twisted-mellin-formula (m = p^n): L(f, χ̄, j+1) = (−2πi)^j/(τ(χ)j!)·Σ_aχ(a)I_j(a/p^n). Then G(χ) = τ(χ) cancels and leaves −(−2πi)^j/(2πi)^{j+1} = (−1)^{j+1}/(2πi).
For n ≥ 1, χ(p) = 0 and L(f_α, χ̄, s) = L(f°, χ̄, s) (p-stabilised-euler-factors), so the formula does not see the stabilization.
acceptance: Pollack–Stevens (1) (§6, p. 27) is the same statement in another normalization: μ_f(z^j·χ) = α^{−n}·p^{n(j+1)}/(−2πi)^j·j!/τ(χ^{−1})·L(f, χ^{−1}, j+1)/Ω_f^±. Since τ(χ)τ(χ^{−1}) = χ(−1)p^n, this is χ(−1)·α^{−n}p^{nj}Σ_aχ(a)I_j(a/p^n)/Ω_f^± = α^{−n}p^{nj}Σ_aχ(a)I_j(−a/p^n)/Ω_f^±. It is the normalization through −a/p^n, and so consistent with B.1 with Ω_{B.1}^ε = −ε(−1)^kΩ_{PS}^ε/(2πi).

Pollack's AWS notes (p. 13): ∫χ dμ_f = α^{−n}τ(χ)L(f, χ̄, 1)/Ω_f^± for k = 0, n ≥ 1, from μ_f(a + p^nℤ_p) built on {a/p^n} − {∞}. This is the normalization through +a/p^n, which for k = j = 0 differs from B.1 by −1/(2πi) and the sign χ(−1) = ε.
Reading B.1 with L(f, χ, j+1), as the stage text transcribes it, would contradict the numerical check of twisted-mellin-formula for non-real χ; for quadratic χ both readings agree.
